title: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant H

parts.title: Part 1.1
parts.instructions: Level A1-A2. Three short personal questions about you and your interests, asked one after another. You have 30 seconds to answer each question. There is no preparation time. Begin speaking when you hear the chime. These are scored items 1-3 (0-5 together).

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant H - PART 1.1 (level A1-A2, scored items 1-3)

EXAMINER, read aloud exactly:
"Part one. In this part, I am going to ask you three short questions about yourself and your interests. And then, you will see some photos and answer some questions about them. You will have 30 seconds to reply to each question. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

[STAGE DIRECTION: play the chime before each question. Ask the three questions one after another. Allow exactly 30 seconds for each answer, then move on even if the candidate is still speaking. Give no preparation time, and do not rephrase a question more than once.]

QUESTION 1 (30 seconds). Tell me a little about your home. Who do you live with, and which room do you use most?

QUESTION 2 (30 seconds). Do you like watching sport, on television or at a stadium? Why, or why not?

QUESTION 3 (30 seconds). Tell me about a film, a song or a television programme that you enjoyed recently.

[STAGE DIRECTION: after the third answer, say "Thank you." and move straight on to Part 1.2.]

parts.title: Part 1.2
parts.instructions: Level B1. Two photographs on one theme and three questions asked one after another. Question 4 asks you to compare the two pictures and you have 45 seconds for it; questions 5 and 6 ask for your opinion and you have 30 seconds for each. There is no preparation time. These are scored items 4-6 (0-5 together).

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant H - PART 1.2 (level B1, scored items 4-6)

EXAMINER, read aloud exactly:
"Now, I am going to ask you to compare two pictures and I will ask you two questions about them. Look at the photographs. What do you see in these pictures?"

[STAGE DIRECTION: show both pictures side by side; if no photographs are available, read the two descriptions below aloud before asking question 4. There is no preparation time. Play the chime before each question.]

[PICTURE 1: a group of about eight teenagers playing five-a-side football on a floodlit outdoor pitch in the evening; the ground is wet and shining, one boy is stretching out a leg for the ball while two others run towards him with their arms raised, and a few friends in winter coats watch from behind a wire fence.]

[PICTURE 2: a young man sitting alone on a sofa late at night, wearing headphones and holding a games controller, his face lit blue by a large screen in front of him; a bowl of crisps, a phone and an empty cup stand on the low table beside him, and the curtains behind him are closed.]

QUESTION 4 (45 seconds). Compare these two pictures. What do you see in them, and how are these two ways of spending an evening different?

QUESTION 5 (30 seconds). Which of these two evenings would you prefer, and why?

QUESTION 6 (30 seconds). Some people say that free time spent with other people is worth more than free time spent alone. Do you agree? Why, or why not?

[STAGE DIRECTION: keep strictly to the times - 45 seconds for question 4, 30 seconds each for questions 5 and 6. Say "Thank you." after the sixth answer and move on to Part 2.]

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: Level B2. One picture and three questions, all shown to you at the same time. You have 1 minute to think before you start speaking and 2 minutes to answer all three questions together. You are not required to describe the picture - it is only there to introduce the theme. This is scored item 7 (0-5).

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant H - PART 2 (level B2, scored item 7)

EXAMINER, read aloud exactly:
"Part two. In this part, I am going to show you a picture and ask you three questions. You will have one minute to think about your answers before you start speaking. You will have two minutes to answer all three questions. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime). Look at the photograph."

[PICTURE: a half-empty municipal sports hall in the middle of a weekday morning; a woman in her fifties is stretching alone on a mat near the wall, while behind her stand an unused badminton net, a stack of plastic chairs and a noticeboard covered with faded timetables.]

[STAGE DIRECTION: show the picture (or describe it aloud) and present all three questions together, on the screen or on a card. Tell the candidate: "You do not have to describe the picture." Then give exactly one minute of silent preparation, play the chime, and time two minutes for all three answers together. Do not interrupt between the questions; if the candidate stops early, wait in silence until the two minutes have passed.]

THE THREE QUESTIONS (given together):
1. Tell me about a sport or a hobby that you once took up. What made you start it, and did you keep it up?
2. How has the way you spend your free time changed you as a person?
3. What factors most influence whether people in general stay active in their free time, or give it up?

[REMINDER TO THE CANDIDATE, if needed: "You have two minutes for all three questions. Describing the picture is not required."]

[STAGE DIRECTION: at two minutes say "Thank you." and move on to Part 3.]

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions:
Level C1. One topic statement with a FOR list and an AGAINST list, three points in each. Choose two points from each list and give a balanced argument representing both sides. You have 1 minute to prepare and 2 minutes to speak. This is the eighth and final scored item of the test.

EXAMINER NOTE - OFFICIAL SCORING:
Eight scored items in total. Items 1-3 (Part 1.1, the three personal questions) are scored together, 0-5. Items 4-6 (Part 1.2, the picture comparison and the two opinion questions) are scored together, 0-5. Item 7 (Part 2) is scored 0-5. Item 8 (Part 3) is scored 0-6. Maximum raw score 21, converted to a rating out of 75.

questions.q:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant H - PART 3 (level C1, scored item 8)

EXAMINER, read aloud exactly:
"Part three. In this part, you are going to speak on a topic for two minutes. You can see the topic on the screen and two lists of points - for and against - related to the topic. Choose two items from each list and give a balanced argument to represent both sides of the topic. You have one minute to prepare your argument. You will then have two minutes to speak. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

TOPIC STATEMENT (show on screen or on a card, and read aloud once):
"A city should pay for its sports halls, swimming pools and concert venues out of public money, rather than leaving them to private companies."

FOR:
 - cheap or free facilities put sport and entertainment within reach of low-income families
 - keeping a population active lowers the cost of treating illness later
 - a public pool or hall brings together neighbours who would otherwise never meet

AGAINST:
 - the same money is needed more urgently by hospitals, schools and transport
 - private clubs are usually better equipped and better run than council ones
 - public facilities are often used by a small, already-active minority

[STAGE DIRECTION: leave the statement and both lists visible throughout. Give exactly one minute of silent preparation - the candidate may make notes. Remind the candidate once, before the chime, that two points must be chosen from each list and that both sides must be represented. Play the chime, then time two minutes. Do not join in the argument. At two minutes say "Thank you. That is the end of the test."]
